name: Questioning Your Own Sources
title: Questioning Your Own Sources
answer: Questioning your own sources is the practice of testing the evidence a literature review rests on before that evidence is used to support a conclusion. It covers the provenance of each cited work, the methods behind its claims, and whether the sources agree or merely appear to. In a review, this means treating the reference list as a set of claims to be checked rather than a foundation to be trusted.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Questioning your own sources is the practice of testing the evidence a literature review rests on before that evidence is used to support a conclusion. It covers the provenance of each cited work, the methods behind its claims, and whether the sources agree or merely appear to. In a review, this means treating the reference list as a set of claims to be checked rather than a foundation to be trusted.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on reference managers, full text databases, and screening tools that track where each paper came from and how it was found.Citation graphs and deduplication tools help, but the underlying record is still the original paper.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A reviewer starts by asking how each source was found, whether it was retrieved through a systematic search or added by hand, and whether the search itself could have missed contrary work. Each claim is then checked against the paper's own methods, sample, and stated limits, not against a summary or a secondary mention. Where sources conflict, the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged away, and any source that cannot be verified is flagged or dropped.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and provenance turn on accurate attribution, respect for publisher terms, and clear separation between a source's words and the reviewer's interpretation. Content on this site never links to the Consensus search tool, it links to the original paper, which keeps the chain from claim to source visible. Retracted papers, corrections, and preprint versions that later changed all need to be caught before they are cited as settled evidence.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward reviews that carry their own audit trail, where every claim shows the paper, the passage, and the check that produced it. Automated claim extraction and screening will make that trail cheaper to build, but they also raise the risk of propagating a bad source at scale. The likely result is more emphasis on provenance as a first class part of the review, not an appendix.
